speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have been experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To understand the underlying cause, please describe the duration and severity of these symptoms, and have you had any recent fevers or changes in bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are concerning for a systemic process like lymphoma. Have you noticed any fevers, and have you experienced any night sweats severe enough to soak your sheets? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and LDH.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: White Blood Cells (WBC) - Elevated; Hemoglobin - Slightly Decreased; Platelets - Normal. LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE (LDH) - Elevated.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a "fixed" and rapidly enlarging supraclavicular node is highly concerning for malignancy. Given your B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and abdominal pain, we need to confirm these findings immediately. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and LDH; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest and Abdomen CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: White Blood Cells (WBC) - Elevated; Hemoglobin - Slightly Decreased; Platelets - Normal. LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE (LDH) - Elevated. CT SCAN THORAX AND ABDOMEN: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma. The combination of B symptoms, elevated LDH, leukocytosis, and the CT scan findings of massively enlarged, fixed lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and mediastinal regions is diagnostic for lymphoma, likely an aggressive subtype such as Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma or Hodgkin Lymphoma.
